_comment: QUESTIONS THE SECTOR HUB REDUCTION RAISED AND DID NOT ANSWER (brief 15).
The brief is a DISPLAY pass: no census file, no scope rule, no ladder script, no
projects.json row and no gated summary moves in it. Where a display need looked like
it needed a data change, the rule is to write the question here and hold -- which is
what each entry below is. None of them is acted on in the pull request that raises
Same shape as sources/cement_ccs_questions.json, and the same rule: a question of this
kind never changes anything by itself. The ruling does, and the ruling is George's.
The question stays in the file after it is answered.
BRIEF 17 ADDS Q5 TO Q10, 12 October 2026, under the same rule. That brief is a
display pass with one hard boundary -- no census file, no gated summary, no scope
rule, no projects.json row, no status_history event and no verdict -- and each
entry below is an item it ran into, could not settle without crossing that
boundary, skipped, and named in its report.

questions.question: IFESTOS holds a SIGNED Innovation Fund grant and its project status is still `announced`. Is the row's status out of date, or is a signed grant compatible with an announced project?
questions.why_the_rules_did_not_settle_it: Brief 15 lists this as a display defect: 'IFESTOS shows funding with status announced while GeZero and ANRAV show funded: render the status group the funding node carries, no exception; if the node's status is what is wrong, that is data and goes to the questions file, not a display patch.' The display half is done -- the hub's project rows now print the figure with the FUNDING node's status group beside it, so all three read `committed` and the project's own status no longer decides how its money is labelled. What is left is the data half, and it is the other way round from the way the brief guessed: the funding nodes agree with each other (innovation-fund-gezero `approved`, innovation-fund-anrav `approved`, innovation-fund-ifestos `signed` -- one status group, committed). It is the PROJECT rows that disagree: gezero-geseke and anrav-devnya moved to `funded`, ifestos-kamari did not, and its status_history holds one event, `announced` on 2023-07-14.
questions.what_a_ruling_would_need_to_say: Whether a signed grant against a project is itself a `funded` event on that project's history -- in which case ifestos-kamari is missing one and the fix is a dated event with its source, not a display change -- or whether the two layers are allowed to disagree because a grant agreement and a company's own announcement are different facts with different sources.
questions.ruling: HELD, AND NOT A DISPLAY PATCH. George, 24 September 2026: IFESTOS is a CENSUS CORRECTION and goes through the census tab with the documents attached. Nothing in this pull request touches the row. The display half stands as built — a project's funding figure carries the status group the FUNDING node holds, so the project's own status no longer decides how its money reads, and all three of IFESTOS, GeZero and ANRAV read `committed`. Whether ifestos-kamari is missing a dated `funded` event is the census's question and is asked there.

questions.question: Diacritics are stripped on some register rows and kept on others. Which spelling is the register's, and do the stripped rows get corrected?
questions.why_the_rules_did_not_settle_it: Brief 15 lists 'diacritics stripped inconsistently on labels' among the display defects to fix in passing. It is not a display defect. Every renderer on the surfaces this pass rebuilds prints the string it is handed, unchanged, and nothing in web/ or in sources/ normalises a label: the one NFKD fold in the tree is sources/dep_sweep.py, which folds a URL for matching and writes nothing to a page. The inconsistency is in the values. 23 of 205 project rows carry diacritics correctly -- Sunwoda Nyiregyhaza is stored 'Nyíregyháza', SVOLT stored 'Überherrn', Gotion InoBat stored 'Šurany', Carbon2Business stored 'Lägerdorf' -- and the rows below, in the same file, are stored folded. So this is data, and by the brief's own rule it is held.

entries.note: the two rows at the same works spell it two different folded ways

entries.stored: Nordion Energi, Goteborg Energi, Renova, Port of Gothenburg
entries.note: and the same city is the English exonym Gothenburg in this row's plant field

questions.what_a_ruling_would_need_to_say: Whether a place or company name is stored as its own language writes it -- which is what the 23 correct rows already do -- and if so whether the folded rows are corrected in this register or left until each is next visited by a census pass. And separately, whether a row may go on using an English exonym in one field and the local name in another, as cinfracap does with Gothenburg and Goteborg.
questions.ruling: HELD, AND NOT A DISPLAY PATCH. George, 24 September 2026: the folded rows are CENSUS CORRECTIONS and go through the census tab with the documents attached — the documents being the point, since which spelling is right is a question about what the company and the municipality write, not about what this register guessed. No renderer is changed: none was wrong.

questions.question: What are 'the coverage link and data alias' the footer row is to carry 'as today'?
questions.why_the_rules_did_not_settle_it: Brief 15 §Spokes and footer: 'Footer row: the three links above, then the coverage link and data alias as today. Nothing else.' The sector hub carries neither today. /coverage is linked from nowhere on the site on purpose -- SiteFooter.tsx says so in its own note, an orphan by decision -- and nothing on this page or any sector page renders anything called a data alias. The three spoke links are built; the two unknowns are not invented.
questions.what_a_ruling_would_need_to_say: Either the two links with their destinations, or that the row is the three spokes and nothing else.
questions.ruling: ANSWERED, AND THE BRIEF WAS WRONG. George, 24 September 2026: the footer row is the three spoke links and nothing else — companies, feed, connections. The coverage link and the data alias belong to the homepage and stay there; the line in brief 15 that put them on the sector hub footer was an error in the brief. This is what the pull request already built, so nothing changes; the question is kept because a reader who finds a three-link footer and a brief asking for five is entitled to see which one was corrected.

questions.question: Where does the COMPLETE list of funding allocations live now?
questions.why_the_rules_did_not_settle_it: The hub used to render every allocation in the sector, in three status groups, with the programme, the amount, the measure it sits under and the project it finances. Brief 15 gives Opportunity a framing line (the committed sum, which is kept) and a capped list, and rules that complete lists live on spokes -- but it gives Opportunity no spoke, and names no other home for the allocation rows. They are not lost: every allocation is on its project's own page and its committed figure is in the projects block and on the projects spoke. They are no longer readable as one list of the sector's money. The Opportunity block's link goes to the support-direction filter on the policies spoke, which is the list of measures that pay rather than the list of allocations.
questions.what_a_ruling_would_need_to_say: Whether the allocation list wants a spoke of its own (/sectors/<slug>/funding), whether it belongs on the projects spoke as a second table, or whether the committed sum plus the per-project figures is the whole of what a reader is owed.
questions.ruling: ANSWERED: NO SPOKE, AND NO LINK. George, 24 September 2026: opportunity gets no spoke page, and the block renders without a link — which is the second of the two things brief 15 allowed, with the pull request stating it. The support-direction filter this pull request had pointed the block at is REMOVED as its destination: a block's link means the complete list of what the block is showing the top of, and the support measures are not that — the framing line counts allocations and the rows are measures, so the link promised the rest of a list the line does not count. The support list stays on the policies spoke under #support, reached by reading that page. Where the complete allocation list eventually lives is still open and is not this brief's to settle.

questions.question: Is the canonical host the apex, `https://eufabric.eu`, or `https://www.eufabric.eu`? Brief 17 §E.1 states www and says 'No change to this'; the repository states the apex in three places and gates it.
questions.why_the_rules_did_not_settle_it: They settle it the other way, which is why this is a question rather than a fix. eufabric-page-specifications.md is the authority for the route list and says 'The canonical origin is the apex, https://eufabric.eu'; web/lib/routes.ts sets SITE_URL to the apex with the reasoning beside it (a sitemap of redirects publishes an address that is not the one that gets indexed); and web/lib/sitemap.test.mts asserts both the value AND that it does not match //www. — an assertion written to catch exactly this change. Brief 17 opens by saying it changes no rule and that the page specifications stand, so the pass kept the apex: moving to www would edit a specification rule, break a gate test, and make every one of the 668 sitemap URLs a redirect unless the edge redirect is flipped in the same change. The edge is not in this repository, which is the other half of why a builder cannot decide this.
questions.what_would_change_it: One line in web/lib/routes.ts, one assertion in web/lib/sitemap.test.mts, one paragraph in eufabric-page-specifications.md §0.8, and the Vercel domain redirect — in that order, together, or not at all.

questions.question: Four project rows render the words `rung` and `ladder` to a reader — five occurrences — from notes on status_history events. Brief 17 §D.9 says surfaces say 'check' and 'checks' and never 'rung' or 'ladder'. May those notes be rewritten, and by whom?
questions.why_the_rules_did_not_settle_it: The display half of §D.9 is clean: no component, no stylesheet and no prose block on the site uses either word, and the only hits are inside note text carried by census rows. A note on a status_history event is a census field, and brief 17's one hard boundary is that nothing in the pass edits a census file or a status_history event. So the words reach a reader and the pass may not touch them. The notes are also not loose prose: each explains why a row sits where it does, in the vocabulary of the confirmation work that put it there, and two of them cite a docket entry. Rewriting them is a census edit with a reviewer, not a display patch.

questions.question: Does /sectors/batsol become /sectors/batteries, and if so what serves the old path? Brief 17 lists the rename as out of scope and asks for it to be raised here with the 308 note if the pass touches the route — which it does: the route now serves nine country views beneath it.
questions.why_the_rules_did_not_settle_it: The slug is a FIGARO industry key and the keying is load-bearing: `batsol` covers batteries AND solar, the ecosystem instance covers batteries only, and solar stays in the register with no ecosystem edge (data/transition/ecosystems.json). Renaming the ROUTE without renaming the key would put a second name on one thing; renaming the key would move an input-output join. What this pass changed is the cost of deciding late: /sectors/batsol now has six spokes and nine country views under it, so the rename is 16 URLs rather than one, and 10 of those 16 are in the sitemap. THE 308 NOTE: a permanent redirect that preserves the method is a 308 and not a 301, and the reason to care is that these URLs are only ever fetched with GET — so either works for a crawler, and a 308 is the one that cannot be degraded to a GET by an intermediary if a form is ever posted to one of them. Whichever is chosen, every old URL has to answer with it rather than 404, and the sitemap has to carry the new one only.

questions.question: The coverage page tells a reader a file had 'Two independent reads, reconciled, rulings docketed'. `reconciled` and `docketed` are on the internal list in sources/display_vocabulary.py. What should those three labels say instead?
questions.why_the_rules_did_not_settle_it: The rule is decidable and the replacement is not. The internal list bans a word because it is precise inside the repository and meaningless outside it, and these three labels are the clearest case on the site: a reader meeting 'rulings docketed' learns that this platform has a docket. But the labels are a claim about METHOD -- how many independent reads a file had and whether their differences were resolved -- and that is the most load-bearing claim the coverage page makes. Paraphrasing it is a judgement about what the reader is being promised, not a word swap. FOUND BY WIDENING THE GATE: check_display_vocabulary.py read web/app and web/components and not web/lib, so the one file where every computed sentence on the site is worded was outside it. This pass added web/lib and these three are what it found that it could not also fix.

entries.label: Two independent reads, reconciled, rulings docketed

questions.question: The site-wide schema.org Dataset description reads 'N measures decoded from M EU acts'. Brief 17 §D.10 says there is to be no acts-decoded counter anywhere. Does 'anywhere' reach structured data?
questions.why_the_rules_did_not_settle_it: The counter is gone from every rendered surface -- the front page line that carried it was removed, the tiles carry no counts, and /sectors carries none -- and this is the only place either number survives. It is also not the same kind of statement: the ruling was that the register should not sell itself on a page about the industries, and a Dataset description is addressed to a crawler and is legitimately about the register. Removing it would change what the site tells search engines it is, which is a positioning decision rather than a display one.

questions.question: Brief 17 §B.2 names '1,980 MW' as the hydrogen drawn figure. The figure computed from data/transition/projects.json is 2,480 MW across 13 drawn rows. Which is meant?
questions.why_the_rules_did_not_settle_it: The rule settles it in favour of the file -- every number in a report is quoted from a gated file (sources/scope.md, 21 September 2026) -- so the standfirst says 2,480 MW and the brief's figure is not used anywhere. The question is kept because the DIFFERENCE is exactly one row: ricenergy-besaya-torrelavega at 500 MW, which 2,480 minus 1,980 is. So 1,980 is not a slip; it is the correct figure for the drawn set as it stood before that row landed, which means the brief was written against an earlier state of the file and any other figure in it may be too.

questions.question: Three cited URLs fail the link gate on main, and two different census decisions are owed. The two Lyten press releases should move to `refused_declared_reader` the moment a person opens them; the CO2LLECT citation should be re-pointed or archived once co2llect.de's English section returns. Who does each, and when?
questions.why_the_rules_did_not_settle_it:
The rules settle what the gate should do and not what the rows should say, and the rows are census. THE FAILURE IS PRE-EXISTING AND REPRODUCIBLE ON MAIN: the same three URLs fail the prebuild chain at 945b58e, so main is red and the pass that found it is a display pass that may not edit a status_history event. What this pass did instead was fix the GATE, twice, in the way the gate's own doctrine already prescribes.

LYTEN: both URLs answer HTTP 403 from Cloudflare, and they answer it to a browser User-Agent exactly as they answer it to the declared reader. That is a CDN refusing this address, which is what BOT_HOSTILE is for and what the elektroniknet.de entry of 19 September records in the same words. No row edited, nothing re-read. The honest end state is `refused_declared_reader` with the day a PERSON opened the page, and nobody has.

CO2LLECT: the page answers 404 and so does every other path under co2llect.de/en/ -- and /en/ ITSELF REDIRECTS to /en/maintenance, while the German root serves normally. The publisher has put its English section under maintenance; it has not removed the page. check_links now asks the path a 404 sits under before declaring the page gone, walking up to the root, and reports with the evidence rather than failing. It fails again the day the section is back, which is the point: if the page does not return, the citation needs re-pointing or archiving, and that is a census decision. The body IS on file -- sources/cache/ccs holds a 200 of 82,603 bytes for it -- so `dead_since` is available to whoever makes it.
